findings.title: Python lint baseline is read eagerly, and the guide does not ship that file
findings.description:
In `LintCheck.python()`, when no `ruff.toml`/`.ruff.toml` exists and `pyproject.toml` has no `[tool.ruff]` section, line 116 evaluates `fs.readFileSync(this.source('python', 'ruff.toml'))` as an argument before `writeOrSuggest` checks `writeLint`. The guide tree in this worktree has `project-documents/ai-project-guide/project-guides/lint/python/required` and nothing else under `python/`. The only `ruff.toml` in the repo is the test fixture's, under `packages/cli/tests/ideInstall/fixture_guide/lint/python/`.

Effect, traced by reading: any project with `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py` or `requirements*.txt` and no ruff config hits an ENOENT on every `cf setup-ide <target>` run, with or without `--write-lint` and with `--dry-run`. `installIde` maps that to a filesystem error and returns exit 1. `setupIdeAction` then throws, so worktree installs and command installs are skipped. `cf init --ide` calls the same path (`init.ts:152`). The root files are already written by then, because `checkLintConfigs` runs after `manifest.finish()`. Skip this with `rules.exclude` containing `python.md`.

Fix: read the baseline only inside the write branch, and when the guide lacks it, fail with an explicit `InstallAbort` that names the missing file.

findings.title: Dry run can write to or delete real project files through symlinks
findings.description:
`copyInstallPaths` uses `fs.cpSync` with `verbatimSymlinks: true` and leaves `dereference` at its default of false. Symlinks are copied as symlinks with their original target text. An absolute link in an install directory, such as `.claude/agents -> /abs/project/shared-agents`, still resolves to the real project from inside the sandbox. The install then writes through it in `installFile` (`manifest.ts:139`) and deletes through it in `finish()` (`manifest.ts:192`), since both resolve the parent directory through the link. The module's own contract says "The project is never touched." `flags.test.ts` checks only plain-file trees, so this path is untested.

Fix: copy with `dereference: true` so the sandbox holds its own bytes. `reportChanges` uses `lstat` on both sides, so it must follow the same rule or the copies will show up as spurious `+` entries.

findings.title: Stale-file deletion lost the containment and non-regular-file guards
findings.description:
The deleted `pruneStaleFiles` (in `worktreePropagation.ts`) rejected manifest paths containing `..` or absolute paths, rejected stale paths whose parent resolved outside the checkout through a symlink, and kept non-regular stale paths. Its test file `worktreePrune.test.ts` pinned all three and was deleted. `InstallManifest.finish()` now does `path.join(this.targetRoot, rel)`, then `isFile` (which follows symlinks), then `rmSync`, with no containment check. `removeEmptyInstallDirs` has the same unchecked path arithmetic. A `../` manifest line whose CRC and size match an outside file would delete that file, and a symlinked stale entry is removed rather than kept. No ideInstall test covers these cases.

Fix: port the lexical and realpath containment checks and the non-regular skip into `finish()`, and restore the three tests against the new module.

findings.title: Required-file parser silently passes requirements it should check
findings.description:
Two paths report a requirement as satisfied when it is not:
1. `toReadLines` drops a final line with no trailing newline, so `missingRequirements` never checks it. `lint.test.ts:107` pins that drop.
2. A line whose first alternative is empty (`|x`) pushes `''` into `missing`, and `join` then makes it indistinguishable from "nothing missing". `lint.test.ts:111` expects `''` and treats it as correct.

CLAUDE.md treats a silent miss on valid input as a bug, and a required file without a final newline is valid input. The shipped `required` files all end with newlines, so this is latent.

Fix: check every non-blank, non-comment line including the last. Throw on a line whose first alternative is empty.

findings.title: The test suite cannot see the real guide's lint path
findings.description:
The real-guide smoke test runs against an empty project. `python()` returns at its project-detection check and never reaches the baseline read. Every lint test uses the fixture guide, which does ship `lint/python/ruff.toml`. That mismatch is why the missing file at `lint.ts:116` passes CI.

Fix: add a real-guide case with a `pyproject.toml` and no ruff config. Assert exit 0, and assert `ruff.toml` is written only with `--write-lint`.

findings.title: Lint file names are spelled out in two places, and one list does nothing
findings.description: `LINT_WRITE_PATHS` repeats the file names that `lint.ts` writes. Lint only writes configs that are absent (`lint.ts:133-136`, `178`, `196`, and the `writeOrSuggest` callers). Copying an absent path into the sandbox does nothing, so the list is never needed. Drop it, or derive it from the write sites.

findings.title: Prompt says files "will be overwritten" but the installer now preserves them
findings.description: Unmanaged `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` are now backed up to `.pre-context-forge` with a managed block appended, and non-owned rule files are skipped with a warning (`manifest.ts:144-174`). The comment at `setup-ide.ts:144-146` describes this, but the prompt still says "will be overwritten." Suggest: "already exist; unmanaged content is kept and backed up to `<name>.pre-context-forge`."

findings.title: Managed-marker detection uses two different match modes
findings.description: The prompt-skip check matches the BEGIN marker as a substring. `managedState` matches it as a whole line. A file with an indented or suffixed BEGIN marker skips the prompt, then fails with the unbalanced-markers message. The failure is loud, not silent, but the two checks disagree. This predates the diff, which now routes both through the same installer. Use one matcher.

findings.title: Harness still parses a `--root` flag that no longer exists
findings.description: `run()` skips the token after `--root` when choosing the target. `flags.test.ts` passes `--root` only as a label, so the flag is dead in the harness. Remove the special case and pass the root directly.

findings.title: `worktreePropagation.ts` no longer propagates anything
findings.description: The module now only filters registered worktrees. Its name, `propagationTargets`, and `worktreePropagation.test.ts` all keep the old "propagation" name. Rename when convenient.

findings.title: No references to the removed copy-and-prune and guide-script symbols remain
findings.description: Searched `packages/` for `readManifest`, `parseManifestLine`, `manifestTempPath`, `ManifestEntry`, `propagateToWorktrees`, `pruneStaleFiles`, `sweepGeneratedPrompts`, `guideScript`, `setupIdeScriptPath`, `propagateDirs`, `generatedPromptDirs` and `--capabilities`. The only hit is a comment in `flags.test.ts`. `init.ts:152` calls `setupIdeAction` and ignores the changed return value.

findings.title: The `getApplyTo` and `replaceBlock` fixes behave as their updated tests claim
findings.description: `getApplyTo` now returns on the closing fence, so the no-paths case gives `**` once. Unclosed frontmatter with paths gives `''`, which matches the documented behavior. `replaceBlock` (`managedSection.ts:112-128`) trims exactly one added newline, and only when the original lacked one. The updated snapshots match that logic.
